title: Microsoft Purview DLP: stop Copilot sending sensitive data to external web search
notes: 2026-11-16: taken offline; the grace for pages published before the check existed is off
summary: Hold: the printed PowerShell rule is incomplete and does not configure the documented web-grounding action, and both admin paths omit documented navigation steps. The licensing and no-meter assertions lack feature-specific support, adaptive DLP scopes are not established, and Microsoft now documents a preview web-search settings API that the table reports as absent.

claims.claim: With web search enabled, Copilot may send a query derived from the prompt to the web search provider.
claims.quote: Based on these terms, Copilot generates a search query that it sends to the Bing search service asking for more information.

claims.claim: The capability provides real-time protection against sensitive data being used for external web search.
claims.quote: This real-time control helps organizations mitigate data leakage and oversharing risks by preventing Microsoft 365 Copilot and agents from using sensitive data for external web search.

claims.claim: The rule detects configured sensitive information types in prompt text at the Copilot policy location.
claims.quote: Add a rule with the Content contains > Sensitive information types condition and choose the SITs you want to detect.

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment
claims.claim: The Performing Web Searches action blocks external web grounding for a prompt matching the configured SITs.
claims.quote: This prevents prompt text that matches the configured SITs from being sent to external search providers for that request.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: After the web-search block, Copilot can still answer using internal Microsoft 365 sources the user can access.
claims.quote: Copilot still returns a response grounded in internal Microsoft 365 data sources where the user has access.

claims.claim: The web-search protection covers Microsoft 365 Copilot, Copilot Chat and Cowork.
claims.quote: Restrict Microsoft 365 Copilot, Copilot Chat, and Cowork from using external web search when prompts contain sensitive data.

claims.claim: The capability extends to Copilot Studio agents published to Microsoft 365 Copilot.
claims.quote: This capability currently extends to Microsoft 365 Copilot and agents built in Copilot Studio that are published to Microsoft 365 Copilot.

claims.claim: The same Copilot DLP location also supports excluding sensitivity-labelled files and emails from processing.
claims.quote: Create DLP policies that use the Microsoft Copilot, Copilot Chat, and Copilot Cowork policy location with the Content contains > Sensitivity labels condition to exclude items from being processed.

claims.claim: The same DLP location supports blocking sensitive prompts.
claims.quote: This feature is in preview and is rolling out to all tenants with access to Microsoft 365 Copilot and Copilot Chat.
claims.fix: Qualify the neighbouring prompt-blocking action as preview; the web-search action's own section is not marked preview.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The web-search restriction is admin-opt-in and does not block grounding until an administrator configures enforcement.
claims.quote: The RestrictWebGrounding parameter specifies an action for the DLP rule that blocks web grounding. Valid values are: $true: Web grounding is blocked. $False: Web grounding isn't blocked. This value is the default.
claims.fix: Add the New-DlpComplianceRule reference to sources; its RestrictWebGrounding parameter explicitly documents the nonblocking default.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model, cost; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: This web-search protection is included in licences already held, justifying licensing.model included and cost none.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot DLP web search licensing; web search DLP no additional license. Opened the feature article and Microsoft Purview service description; the latter distinguishes prompt safeguards from file/email protection but does not explicitly identify this web-search action's entitlement.
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to unknown and cost to low for the documented administrative work until an explicit entitlement for this action is established. State that feature-specific licensing is Not yet published and remove the assertion that existing Purview DLP entitlements establish inclusion.

claims.where: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing: entitlement bullet
claims.claim: The web-search action requires Microsoft 365 E5, E5 Compliance or Purview Suite plus Microsoft 365 Copilot or Copilot Chat.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot DLP web search licensing E5; web search Purview licensing DLP safeguard. Opened feature Licensing and Purview service description. No passage assigns this SKU requirement to the web-search action; prompt safeguards are listed for all Copilot and Copilot Chat users.
claims.fix: Remove the E5/E5 Compliance/Purview Suite prerequisite for this action. Link https://learn.microsoft.com/office365/servicedescriptions/microsoft-365-service-descriptions/microsoft-365-tenantlevel-services-licensing-guidance/microsoft-purview-service-description and explain that its file/email and prompt entitlements differ, without transferring either to this action without explicit confirmation.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: No metered cost
claims.claim: There is no metered cost for the feature.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot DLP web search metered licensing; Copilot web search DLP no additional license. Opened feature Licensing and Microsoft Purview service description. Neither states that this web-search action is unmetered.
claims.fix: Replace 'No metered cost' with 'No meter is documented for this web-search action at the time of writing (November 2026)'; do not turn the documentation gap into a guarantee of no charge.

claims.claim: The Purview path is Data Loss Prevention > Policies > + Create policy > Custom > location Microsoft Copilot, Copilot Chat, and Copilot Cowork.
claims.quote: Select the Custom template, then Custom policy. On the Locations page, set the Microsoft Copilot, Copilot Chat, and Copilot Cowork location to on.
claims.fix: Use 'Data Loss Prevention > Policies > + Create policy > Custom > Custom policy > Locations > Microsoft Copilot, Copilot Chat, and Copilot Cowork'. The pre-check's missing phrase is not an invented location, but the path does omit Custom policy and the Locations page.

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls: first row and following prose
claims.claim: The printed New-DlpCompliancePolicy and bare New-DlpComplianceRule -RestrictAccess calls create the Performing Web Searches policy and rule.
claims.quote: The RestrictWebGrounding parameter specifies an action for the DLP rule that blocks web grounding. Valid values are: $true: Web grounding is blocked.
claims.fix: Keep the policy-creation call only as policy scaffolding, with a correctly supplied Locations value. Replace the rule fragment with 'New-DlpComplianceRule -Name <rule> -Policy <policy> -ContentContainsSensitiveInformation @(@{Name="<SIT name>"}) -RestrictWebGrounding $true' and cite this rule reference. RestrictAccess requires a hashtable array, not a bare switch; Name and Policy are mandatory, and the cited policy example configures labelled-content exclusion rather than this web-search action.

claims.claim: Purview Data Security AI Administrator is a documented role that can manage these policies.
claims.quote: Purview Data Security AI Admin - Role for editing Data Loss Prevention policies related to Copilot and viewing AI content in Data Security Posture Management.
claims.fix: Replace 'Purview Data Security AI Administrator' with the documented role name 'Purview Data Security AI Admin' in the front matter and rendered table.

claims.claim: An authorised administrator can create a tenant-wide Copilot DLP policy.
claims.quote: An unrestricted administrator can scope policies to administrative units or keep Full directory to apply a policy across the organization.

claims.claim: The exact Microsoft 365 Apps admin center path is Cloud Policy > Allow web search in Copilot.
claims.quote: Under Customization, select Policy Management. On the Policy configurations page, select Create.
claims.fix: Replace the shorthand with the documented navigation: 'Customization > Policy Management > Policy configurations > Create > Start with the basics > Choose the scope > Configure Settings > Allow web search in Copilot'. Add the Cloud Policy overview as the path's docs link/source and retain manage-public-web-access for the setting's behaviour.

claims.where: controls[1].api; Governance controls: second-row API absence
claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented an API surface for the Allow web search in Copilot control.
claims.quote: microsoft.copilot.allowwebsearch | Allow web search in Copilot
claims.fix: Document the preview tenant-only API separately from group-scoped Cloud Policy: PATCH https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/policySettings/microsoft.copilot.allowwebsearch, with the required value request-body property, citing https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/api/admin-settings/copilotpolicysetting-update. State that group/user policies are unsupported by this API, only delegated work/school permission CopilotPolicySettings.ReadWrite is supported, it is global-service only, and beta production use is unsupported. Do not present it as a group-policy equivalent.
